item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q005_cupredoxin_function_transfer","answer":"SCOPe places these domains in the all-β cupredoxin-like fold (b.6) and, more strongly, in the Cupredoxins superfamily (b.6.1), indicating probable remote common ancestry rather than mere topological resemblance. They remain distinct families: plastocyanin/azurin-like domains (b.6.1.1) are the classical type-1 copper proteins, whereas ephrin ectodomains and the PAD4 N-terminal domain are separate functional lineages. Therefore, copper binding and electron-transfer activity must not be transferred from plastocyanin/azurin to an ephrin or PAD4 domain. Those functions require independent evidence such as conservation and geometry of the copper-coordinating residues, direct metal-binding or spectroscopic measurements, redox characterization, and an electron-transfer assay. A cupredoxin template may support modeling of the shared β-sandwich core, but family-specific templates and domain context are required for loops, binding sites, and functional annotation; a convenient SCOPe representative is not automatically a functional representative.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
